mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to turn negative due to tightened financing conditions for corporate investment.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite the rate increase, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a two-sample test across 10 such events.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in unemployment benefits applications (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in consumer demand indicators (HOUST) predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to weaker consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > (lag(PAYEMS) + 10% ) AND HOUST < (lag(HOUST) - 5%) over the next 2 months
regime_hint: Labor market slackening with weak demand
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during the identified interaction window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in retail sales (not directly observable in the given catalog, but proxy via INDPRO rising above 108) coincides with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO falling below 108), signaling a demand shift toward services and away from manufacturing, which predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns in the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO crosses above 108 AND INDPRO < (lag(INDPRO) + 1) within 1 trading day
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative or not statistically different from baseline (p > 0.05) during the interaction window.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive 2-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 107, followed by a rebound above 107, predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as the market anticipates an end to supply disruptions.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 107 for 2 consecutive months AND INDPRO > 107 in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative or the pattern recurs more than twice in a 12-month window without positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.3% in a single month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return turns negative due to market anticipation of future inflation pressures.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during such inflation events.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment (UNRATE > 4%) over the next quarter is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns of 20 days as investor sentiment deteriorates on labor market weakness.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during the regime and statistically significant (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in manufacturing activity (RSAFS < 500 million dollars) followed by a recovery to levels above 520 million in the next month predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as the market anticipates supply chain normalization.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 520 AND RSAFS > 500 within the next month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain negative or the pattern recurs without positive returns in >50% of such events.

mechanism_narrative: During a prolonged period of low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 257) and low federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS < 1.5%), the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive as the market anticipates future rate cuts and accommodative policy.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 257 AND FEDFUNDS < 1.5 for at least 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a regression with controls.
